title: Human PR review methodology
lines: The human PR review methodology rates every file in a large PR/module, skips what carries no review risk, and groups the writeup by risk level instead of file order.

The human review rubric does not apply to AI-driven reviews (/code-review, ultrareview); those run their own findings-based process over the full diff and must not skip or pre-filter files by this rubric.

Importance level 1 (skip/skim) covers pure types, Zod/interface schemas, CRUD boilerplate, default-object factories, narrowing helpers, and lookup/mapping tables with no branching, because the TS compiler and the schema already guard correctness.

Importance level 2 (worth a read) covers small or low-risk logic: status/display-class mapping functions, small encode/decode helpers, data tables where a duplicate or wrong entry has real effect (e.g. a keybinding table), and schema/contract files with wide blast radius.

Importance level 3 (review carefully) covers real logic matching the repo's unit-test carve-out in CLAUDE.md: parsers/splitters with interacting rules, byte-level codecs, pagination/cursor arithmetic, round-trip encode/decode of credentials or sensitive data, and invariant-enforcing builders.
Unit tests (*.test.ts, *_test.go, etc.) are never reviewed and never listed with a rating in the human review.

Generated code (e.g. packages/shared/protocol/wire/*.ts, anything a scripts/generate-*.sh produces) is never reviewed or rated; only check that the generated output matches its source schema after a regen.

In the review writeup, files are grouped by importance level; level 1 files are listed together with the shared pattern stated once, while level 2 and 3 files get one line each saying what the logic does and why it's risky.
Always report the split of files worth reviewing versus reviewable total (e.g. "9 files worth your time out of 40 reviewable") in the review writeup, so the reviewer sees the filtering.

title: Invariants
lines: The renderer must never import a DB driver or parse a wire protocol.
The grid must not create a DOM node per cell for off-screen rows; it is virtualized in both axes.
Row data must not use Vue reactivity; rows live in plain frozen typed structures, the grid reads them imperatively and re-renders on an explicit version counter.
Virtualize long lists too (tree, log panel, document view).
Every operation exceeding ~150 ms must show progress and a working stop button.
Every DB read must go through the cache layer; a cache miss is the only thing that produces a query.

Bulk data is produced and encoded exactly once, in the process that owns the window: a result page is built in Go by the adapter that read it, held in the Go-side L2 cache as native structures, and serialized once when a renderer asks for it.
Go parses every data-plane request envelope, since it answers them; there is no second process, intermediate encoding or re-decode.

The single-encode rule replaces the Electron-era rule (bulk data skips the main process via MessagePort) and the P58a–P58e interim rule (Go forwards without looking); P58f M10 removed the Node engine child, so no Node-served kind exists beside a Go-native one.

The renderer loads no remote content, opens no window, and navigates nowhere but its own base URL. Under Wails only the code-level half holds: no navigation policy remains to stop such a call, whereas Electron's shell enforced it.

Open a second window (Window → New Window, ⇧⌘N) only from a Go-side menu command, never from a renderer-initiated call; JavaScriptCanOpenWindowsAutomatically is Disabled and the renderer must never call window.open or an equivalent.
The update-availability check and install are Go-side: internal/appupdate fetches GitHub's release metadata itself, and InstallUpdate stages the update through its own detached installer.
The renderer calls two nullary update methods (Status, InstallUpdate) and neither sends nor receives a URL.

title: Per-engine adapter facts / PostgreSQL / MariaDB / MySQL
lines: The PostgreSQL, MariaDB and MySQL adapters are full read/write SQL adapters using keyset pagination on the primary key (falling back to LIMIT/OFFSET) and cancelling queries on a side connection via pg_cancel_backend (Postgres) or KILL QUERY (MySQL family).

The PostgreSQL adapter is Go-native (apps/kira-studio/internal/adapters/postgres/, pgx/v5) and is served in-process by adapterhost.Router through the loaders registry; no Node engine child exists any more.

Never pass the caller's op-cancellation context.Context to pgx's own Query/Exec, because pgx honours context cancellation and would race its own cancel request against the adapter's explicit pg_cancel_backend; use adapters.RunWithAbortRace (internal/adapters/abort.go).

MariaDB and MySQL are Go-native (apps/kira-studio/internal/adapters/mysqlfamily/, github.com/go-sql-driver/mysql); mysqlfamily/ holds the single shared Adapter implementation, while mariadb/ and mysql/ each hold only their own Profile (server label, ApplyEngineOptions).

mysqlfamily never passes the op's own context to the driver, because cancelling the context given to QueryContext/ExecContext closes the underlying connection (driver: bad connection on the next statement); it uses adapters.RunWithAbortRace with a background context and an explicit KILL QUERY <threadId> on a side connection.

Versus the Node adapter, the Go MySQL-family adapter loses the query console's "N row(s) affected" status text (a generic "OK" shows instead), because the QueryContext path needed by the multi-statement runner has no RowsAffected(); this is inherent to go-sql-driver/mysql.

The Go MySQL-family adapter has no equivalent of allowPublicKeyRetrieval: when caching_sha2_password needs the server's RSA public key and TLS is off, go-sql-driver requests it unconditionally over plaintext, with no option to refuse.

title: Caching
lines: L1 metadata cache (databases, schemas, tables, columns, PK/FK, indexes, object definitions) is persisted in metadata_cache, survives restart, and has no TTL; staleness is defined by connection epoch, not a clock.

An L1 payload is fresh if written after its connection was most recently established, otherwise stale; a stale payload is bypassed and re-fetched on its first read per kind, and not re-fetched again for the rest of that connection session.

The L1 epoch is ConnectionState.Since; it is compared against a per-kind timestamp stored in payload_json under the reserved key fetchedAt, while the fetched_at column only orders the 200-row eviction.

While a connection is not connected no epoch exists, so the L1 cache serves at any age; this makes the panel instant on launch and lets a SQL console over a cached container offer completion with no live connection.
Connecting no longer deletes the connection's L1 rows (it did through P23); it moves the epoch so rows are re-read lazily, once each, only for paths a user opens.
An explicit Refresh still deletes L1 rows: a node's Refresh drops that node's whole row (all four kinds), and a connection's Refresh or Refresh all drops every row for that connection.

metadata_cache's unique index is (connection_id, path), and the kinds children/describe/definition/columns merge into one row per path; columns (SchemaColumns) is keyed on the container (database/schema node) and fetched in one round trip.

The columns kind is merged into one row per container rather than one row per relation, because per-relation rows would compete with the tree's children rows for the 200-row-per-connection budget on a large schema.

The columns kind follows the same connection-epoch freshness rule, is refreshed on explicit Invalidate, and is readable with no live connection since a cache hit is served before the connection is checked.

The columns cache backs the SQL console's schema-aware completion/diagnostics/hover (state/schemaColumns.ts) automatically when a console or data tab opens over a cached container; the completion layer itself never opens a connection or fetches on its own.

L1 freshness is tracked per kind inside a shared row: refreshing a container's children never freshens its columns, and vice versa; the per-kind fetchedAt map exists because the row-level fetched_at column cannot express this.

L2 result-page cache is an in-memory LRU in the engine, byte-budgeted (default 64 MB, configurable), keyed by hash of {connectionId, path, filter, projection, sort, pageSize, pageToken}, and never persisted.
L2 is invalidated by manual refresh, any local mutation on the same target, and disconnect.
L3 counts cache {connectionId, path, filter} → {count, at} with a 5 min TTL, and is marked stale (greyed with refresh affordance) immediately after any local mutation.
Counts compute only on explicit user request, never automatically, because they are the most expensive read in the app.

No speculative fetching: a page loads only in direct response to a user action (Next/Previous, filter/sort/projection change, Refresh, Count button); background prefetch and automatic count-on-open were removed at user request as unwanted background work, not kept as an opt-out setting.
The settings Cache pane shows usage, hit rate and a Clear caches action.

The renderer keeps a fourth, deliberately unbudgeted cache: five page stores (one per page kind, one loaded page per open tab) plus views/shared/document/rows.ts's parsed-tree cache, released on tab close and pruned to the rendered window on scroll in all five stores.

The renderer cache has no byte budget by deliberate decision: evicting a cold tab's page was declined twice, trading RAM for the ≤ 50 ms cached-tab-switch interaction budget (docs/PERF.md §2.2 lever L-B); ten tabs of large pages mean uncapped renderer memory.
The follow-up for renderer memory is to surface the figure next to the Cache pane's usage, not eviction, handed to P7 (HISTORY.md v1.1 P5 §8 OQ-2).
The renderer caches bridge-fetched server state with TanStack Query, one QueryClient per window (packages/workbench/src/state/queryClient.ts).

API client data (collections tree, saved HTTP/gRPC requests, variables, environments, active environment) are query entries in apiQueries.ts with staleTime: Infinity: never refetched on a timer, only invalidated.

Go broadcasts kira:api:dataChanged on every API-data mutation (emitApiData in bridge/apidata.go) with a batch of {kind, ...scope} changes; the boot-time listener maps each to queryClient.invalidateQueries, so every window refetches exactly the changed scopes.
draftMerge.ts keeps an unsaved edit in the active window from being clobbered by the refetch after an API-data change.

P175 moved jar cookies (['httpJarCookies', url]), history lists and snapshots ([domain, itemId, scratchTabId], [domain+'Snapshot', id]) and gRPC schema (['grpcSchema', 'proto'|'reflection', ...], mirroring Go's descriptor cacheKey) onto TanStack Query.
Pinia stores keep UI state only; server state lives in TanStack Query, and refreshing lazily while a pane is hidden (P8 D11) is each query's enabled flag.
Mutations must call cancelQueries after the bridge call and before setQueryData, so an in-flight list fetch cannot resurrect a deleted row.

internal/httpclient/cookiejar is a fork of Go 1.27.1's net/http/cookiejar (BSD-3 LICENSE kept) because the stdlib jar cannot list or delete; it adds Entries/Delete in entries.go, and Delete removes by exact domain, path and name.
On a Go upgrade, re-copy the cookiejar's jar.go, punycode.go and their tests, then reapply the ascii import path change, the only difference from upstream.

Dotenv parsing (BulkVariablesEditor, dotenv.ts): an inline comment starts at whitespace plus #; a quoted value counts only when the closing quote is followed by nothing or a comment; an unmatched quote makes an unquoted value, never an error.

title: UI architecture / Copy and i18n (P265)
lines: All user-visible text lives in one catalog, packages/theme/src/i18n/en.json; vue-i18n 11 (Composition API, JIT compile, no eval) is the runtime, and Go reads the same file for native text.
A locale is a second file next to en.json; only English ships.

The global typed t(key, params?) uses MessageKey, every leaf path of en.json; an unknown key fails vue-tsc/tsgo. A numeric params.count formats with locale digit grouping and selects the plural branch.
Components must import t from '@theme/i18n' and never use $t or useI18n() outside the i18n folder (U68).

CatalogText puts an element inside a sentence via named slots, so a sentence never splits across literals. Import it from @theme/i18n/CatalogText.vue, not the @theme/i18n index, because the index must stay free of .vue so workers and Node test code can import it.
Run app.use(i18n) at every createApp site: Studio, Space, mobile, git-ui mount(), bootstrapShell, Monaco review zones, because CatalogText needs it.
Call t() at render or call time, never at module scope (U70). In hot paths (SlickGrid formatters, virtual rows, Monaco decorations) resolve once per setup or render pass, never per cell.
Never translate values that drive logic (enum values, status ids, persisted strings, testids); translate only the label shown for them.

In test builds (Studio and Space, under __KIRA_DEBUG_HOOKS__) installCopyTestHook() sets window.__kiraSetLocale('en' | 'pseudo'); pseudo wraps each message as ⟦…⟧, and copyCoverage.ts (setPseudoLocale, expectCatalogText) fails on visible letters outside a marker. Mobile has no test hooks; the static guard covers it.
Catalog keys follow <namespace>.<area>.<surface>.<element>.<role>, camelCase segments, depth 3-6, named for meaning and never for the English text.
Key namespaces are automations, backend, common, docker, format, git, memory, mobile, shared, space, studio, theme, workbench.

Key roles are label, tooltip, aria, placeholder, title, option, status, announce, confirm, body, hint, description, emptyHint, error, empty, loading, example. Confirm groups are <surface>.<x>Confirm.{title,body,confirm}.
Identical text is one key (C3). Put shared vocabulary in common.*, or <namespace>.common.* inside a module; format.* holds behaviour/format.ts word templates.
Copy uses sentence case everywhere (capitals only for first word, proper nouns, acronyms); the native macOS menu (backend.menu.*) is title case.
Put the one-character ellipsis '…' on an action only when it opens a dialog or picker needing more input. Loading text always ends with '…'; placeholders never do.

Labels, buttons, menu items, tooltips, titles, placeholders, options, status words and announcements have no trailing period. Sentences (body, hint, description, emptyHint, error) end with '.', and confirm titles end with '?'.
Use typographic quotes “ ” around a named instance and ’ in contractions; never straight quotes.
Use contractions can’t, couldn’t, isn’t; cannot and could not are banned. Use British spelling (colour, cancelled, behaviour).
Copy must not use '&', '(s)', 'e.g.', an 'Error:' prefix, or OK/Yes/No buttons (use the verb). Use ' — ' between clauses and ': ' before backend error detail.
Counts with a noun are plural messages with {count}; sizes, dates and durations come from behaviour/format.ts.
Name placeholders in camelCase; a user-provided name in prose is “{name}”. Resolved script variables keep VarText inside a CatalogText slot. Never build a string by concatenating translated parts.
An icon-button tooltip and aria-label share one key (.tooltip), worded as the action label, with no shortcut text.

Confirm dialogs: title is '<Verb> <object>?'; body names the instance in “ ” and states the consequence; irreversible actions add common.confirm.irreversible; buttons are Cancel plus the title’s verb.
Empty states read 'No <items> yet' when the user can create one, else 'No <items>'; filtered-empty is 'No matches'.
Error wording: action failed is 'Couldn’t <verb> <object>.' or '…: {error}'; a blocked precondition is 'Can’t <verb>: <reason>.'; a QueryState load failure is 'Couldn’t load' plus 'Retry'.
Status words are short sentence-case phrases; raw engine states (Docker running, plan node names) are data and shown as is.
Glossary: Delete destroys a stored item; Remove detaches while the item survives; Clear empties a list or field; Close ends a transient surface; Dismiss removes a notice.
Glossary: abandon a dialog with Cancel (also for confirm cancel), never Keep or Leave it. Toggle a persistent part with Show <x> / Hide <x>.
Glossary: dropping unsaved changes is Discard / Discard changes, not Revert (a git word); Revert and Reset are for git revert/reset; settings to default is 'Reset to default'.

Glossary: Save persists; Apply applies pending changes while staying open (not Confirm or OK); Create is the creation dialog primary; New <thing>… for menu/toolbar; Add <thing> appends in an editor or list (no + prefix); Import <thing>… imports.

Glossary: re-fetch is Refresh (not Reload); re-attempt is Retry (not Try again); execute once is Run; long-running processes use Start / Stop; undoing an in-progress git operation is Abort; taking over an agent run is 'Take over'.
Glossary: Choose in a picker (not Pick); Select in a list; Edit (not Update, which is reserved for app update); Settings / Open settings (not Preferences).
Glossary: copy actions are 'Copy <thing>', 'Copy as <format>', 'Copy for agent'; copy feedback uses whole messages (Copied name, Couldn’t copy: {error}), not noun fragments.
Glossary: git checkout is 'Check out' as a verb and 'checkout' as a noun, never 'Checkout' as a verb.

Glossary: loading text is 'Loading…' or 'Loading <noun>…'; empty is 'No <items> yet', 'No <items>' or 'No matches', not 'Nothing to show'; failures are 'Couldn’t <verb> <object>: {error}', not 'Failed to' or 'Could not'.

Glossary: irreversible notice is 'This can’t be undone.'; 'Show more' reveals capped items while 'Load more' fetches the next page; terms: repository (not repo), folder (not directory, except working directory), ID, for example.

Catalog checker scripts/copy/check-catalog.ts (rules in catalogRules.ts) runs in bun run lint and enforces C1–C11: message syntax, key shape and role, duplicates, near-duplicates, banned forms, sentence case, punctuation by role, plural shape, placeholder names, unused keys, empty values. ALLOWED_DUPLICATES is empty and each entry needs a reason.
Catalog rule C8 requires plural shape and only named placeholders in backend.*; C10 flags unused keys (--unused, on in lint) and scans internal/ Go callers for backend.*.

Source guard scripts/copy/check-copy.ts (Babel and @vue/compiler-sfc ASTs) runs in bun run lint and enforces U64 template text, U65 static text attribute, U66 string literal in template expression, U67 string in text property or announce call, U68 vue-i18n outside i18n folder, U69 concatenated translation, U70 t( at module scope, U71 t params differing from message placeholders.

Copy-guard exemptions live in scripts/copy/exemptions.ts, one rule for one file with a reason; a stale exemption (no hit left) fails. They cover only font names, protocol tokens, command syntax, EJSON syntax and CLI flag names. 'bun scripts/copy/check-copy.ts --all' prints every hit.

title: Stack (rows Shell to Frontend library baseline)
lines: The desktop shell is Wails v3 (v3.0.0-beta.28) in Go, targeting macOS 14+ on arm64 only.

The window uses a custom hidden-inset title bar (Mac.TitleBar: application.MacTitleBarHiddenInset) drawn by packages/workbench/src/components/TitleBar.vue over a full-size-content window, not the OS-drawn bar.
Each app's frontend/src/workbench/TitleBar.vue supplies its title-bar buttons and mode tabs through the shared shell TitleBar's default slot.
TypeScript is pinned to 6 (below TS 7) on purpose: TS7 ships no stable programmatic compiler API until 7.1, and vue-tsc (run by typecheck:web:studio) consumes that API in-process.

The tsgo binary from @typescript/native-preview (used by typecheck:tests:studio and typecheck:unit:studio) is a separate, already-latest-upstream tool; the plan is to converge on one toolchain once TS 7.1 ships and vue-tsc adopts it.
Bun is the package manager, script runner and test runner; it is tooling only, since every adapter is native Go and nothing at runtime depends on it.

The renderer is built with Vite from apps/kira-studio/frontend/src into frontend/dist, which apps/kira-studio/main.go embeds via //go:embed all:frontend/dist and serves through Wails' AssetOptions.Handler.
The SQL Format button in the query console reaches sql-formatter only through a dynamic import in views/console/sqlFormatterEntry.ts, giving a lazy chunk of about 37 KB gzip.

@faker-js/faker/locale/en is reached through two duplicated one-line entry files, views/grid/fakeData/fakerEntry.ts and packages/api-core/src/http/dynamic/fakerEntry.ts, because packages/api-core is a no-app-import package (P12 D16(e)) and P1 D7 has a biome rule.

Rolldown folds the two identical faker entry files into one shared stub chunk and puts the locale data in its own shared chunk (en-*.js, about 155 KB gzip), the same bytes as the old single fakerEntry chunk.
packages/api-core/src/http/dynamic/generators.ts, a 58-entry $name to faker-call dispatch table, gets its own lazy chunk of about 0.8 KB gzip.

monaco-editor is loaded lazily via a dynamic import in packages/workbench/src/editor/monacoEntry.ts through the shared loadMonaco() in packages/workbench/src/editor/monaco.ts; apps/kira-space/frontend/src/views/repo/monaco.ts re-exports it unchanged.

Every CodeMirror mount in the app, including the SQL console and project/SchemaDialog.vue's DDL editor, sits behind the same memoised Monaco import, so a session opening no editor fetches nothing and the first editor pays the chunk once.

Measured in v1.9 P109 with bun run build:studio, monacoEntry-*.js is 3 819.42 kB raw / 974.99 kB gzip, its CSS 161.81 kB raw / 24.56 kB gzip, and editor.worker-*.js 300.37 kB raw, loaded as a Worker script.

Each Monaco language's Monarch grammar data is in its own lazy sub-chunk (0.4-3.7 KB gzip), fetched only when a file of that language is opened; kira-mongo and kira-redis were transliterated from the CodeMirror StreamLanguages they replace.
The @codemirror/merge chunk (views/httprequest/mergeEntry.ts) was removed: P60a moved the response-history Compare dialog onto Monaco's diff editor and deleted the dependency.
The four remaining lazy chunks are fetched on first use; none costs a launch or grows index-*.js by anything but each phase's own eager app code.

index-*.js fell from 1 723.09 kB raw / 520.66 kB gzip to 1 307.65 kB raw / 384.15 kB gzip when P60b removed nine @codemirror/* packages plus @lezer/highlight, which had been eagerly bundled in the main chunk.
The Vite 8.3.0 bump (P61) moved index-*.js to 1 315.59 kB raw / 387.37 kB gzip through a Rolldown chunking shift, with no code change.
After the P98-P112 frontend-library migration (Pinia, TanStack Query, shadcn-vue, reka-ui) and P100's git-ui removal, index-*.js measures 1 339.31 kB raw / 355.29 kB gzip (v1.9 P109).
The UI uses Vue 3 with script setup and the Composition API in VDOM mode; Vapor mode was evaluated and declined in P6.
Styling uses Tailwind v4 with CSS-first config.
Dynamic colours must be Record<Enum,string> class maps of full literals, never template-built class names, because Tailwind emits only scanned literals.
ADE tones are @theme tokens defined in ade/v2/tones.css.

Every palette colour mark must go through colorMarkClass(mark, color) in packages/theme/src/connColor.ts: rail on left-panel rows, bar on tabs, dot inline, band under view toolbars; no colour leaves the slot empty, and a dot shows a ring.

When converting off plain CSS, stop at the first fit: (1) Tailwind default-scale utility; (2) existing @theme token utility backed by a --kira-* property; (3) new @theme token only if the value recurs 3+ times or is a deliberate design seam; (4) arbitrary value only for a one-off or genuinely runtime/viewport/calc value, with a stated reason.
Define each @theme name once; never re-declare a name that shadcn-bridge.css already owns, because Tailwind v4 resolves a name declared twice to the definition loaded last.

base.css's duplicate --color-muted/--color-input/--color-border declarations were deleted (each now declared only in shadcn-bridge.css) and legacy meanings moved to bg-field and text-muted-foreground; the shadowing had made bg-muted render #9d9d9d instead of #313131.
scripts/check-theme-classes.sh, run as part of bun run lint, guards retired class names (the p-* family, legacy text-muted/bg-input names, retired kui-* selectors) from coming back.
A DialogContent with no explicit width spans the viewport minus 2rem (P110 B9 removed shadcn's default sm:max-w-sm), so every dialog sets its own w-N.

scripts/check-class-conflicts.ts (bun run lint) parses every .vue under app/theme/workbench trees, resolves static class plus conditional :class literals through cn/twMergeKv, and fails on a surviving static duplicate or a conditional literal dropping a static token; it skips elements whose :class root is itself a cn/twMergeKv call.

A registration self-check reads the @theme blocks of tailwind-core.css and git-ui's git.css and asserts every new @theme token (colour, spacing, radius, shadow, animation, leading) wins a same-group merge, so a token not wired into the merge group fails lint.

Each colour/radius value has one canonical kira name repo-wide, including components/ui; shadcn-alias/kira pairs (background/bg, card/elevated, muted/field, input/border-strong, ring/focus, accent/hover, destructive/error, rounded-sm/md/lg/xl / rounded-kira-xs/sm/kira/pill) collapse onto the kira name, because no CSS custom property is set at runtime.
shadcn-bridge.css's @theme inline keeps exactly --color-primary, --color-primary-foreground, --color-muted-foreground and --color-border, and no --radius-* at all.
check-theme-classes.sh's check_alias guard never excludes components/ui and is never extended to git-ui; it keeps retired aliases from returning.
alertVariants in packages/theme/src/components/ui/alert/ has no err key; every error alert uses variant="error" (P263).
Every spinner uses animate-spin (1s); the second 0.7s animate-kira-spin timing was retired.
ResizeHandle is the only splitter mechanism (P264); reka's Splitter* and the Resizable* wrappers are gone.

focus-ring in packages/theme/src/base.css is the only focus-ring definition; the base :focus-visible rule applies it to every natively focused element, and a component opts out only with outline-none when an ancestor draws the ring (InputGroup).

A base-layer * rule sets outline-color/width/offset on every element at rest so :focus-visible only flips outline-style, preventing transition-colors/transition-all from animating the ring from currentcolor/medium/0px on focus (P130).
tabChipVariants (UI/tabs/index.ts) is the only tab-chip class definition.

ToggleGroup defaults outline groups to connected (spacing 0) and default groups to 2px-spaced chips, every item rounded-kira-sm; toggle-group selectors key on reka's data-orientation, never Base UI's data-horizontal/data-vertical (P121).
Chrome uses only the four-value type scale text-kira-sm/md/lg/xl (P123): sm for secondary/caption/status-bar, md for default/control/body, lg for headings, xl for hero titles only.
Tailwind's stock text-xs…text-9xl scale and the retired xs step are reset with --text-*: initial on the @theme root, and check-theme-classes.sh's check_font_scale guards against their return.
Data views (SQL/document/git grids, Monaco, status-bar/tab dirty-dot glyphs) keep their own fixed or Data-font-size-tracking sizes, outside the chrome type scale by design.
packages/theme/src/tailwind-core.css is the host-neutral Tailwind entry (P131 Part 1); base.css is a thin @import of it plus Kira-app-only @theme tokens.

Frontend library baseline: Vue 3.5 + Vite; Tailwind v4 CSS-first with --kira-* bridged in base.css; shadcn-vue on Reka UI bridged in shadcn-bridge.css; Pinia for client state; TanStack Query for server state; VueUse for DOM composables; @tanstack/vue-virtual for row virtualization.
P98 wired only dependencies and bootstrap; P99 migrated the app's 39 reactive() state modules and 200 .vue files onto the new libraries.
Each app creates one Pinia instance (frontend/src/state/pinia.ts) and one QueryClient/VueQueryPlugin in main.ts, with the client from packages/workbench/src/state/queryClient.ts.

P104 deleted all 20 hand-rolled theme/primitives/* components and repointed call sites at components/ui/* (shadcn-vue on Reka UI), or inlined Tailwind composition over those parts for bespoke layout containers (PanelShell, ViewChrome, ViewHeader, ReconnectGate, RunState, ColorPicker).
The v-tooltip directive and the document-level singleton AppTooltip.vue were replaced by the Tooltip/TooltipTrigger/TooltipContent trio, where TooltipProvider owns delay/rearm.
PanelSplitter, VirtualList and TreeHost were replaced by reka's Splitter* (later narrowed to the Resizable wrappers only in P110 iter2) and @tanstack/vue-virtual.
Raw spacing/sizing values were converted onto Tailwind's default numeric scale; only runtime-settable (Appearance) and z-index tokens stay var-backed/bracketed.

There are 20 fetched components/ui/* sets: alert, badge, button, checkbox, command, dialog, dropdown-menu, empty, field, input, input-group, label, native-select, popover, resizable, separator, textarea, toggle, toggle-group, tooltip; each has a real consumer or is deleted.
CommandPalette.vue is built on ui/command, where reka's Listbox owns filtering and keyboard navigation.
ui/scroll-area and ui/context-menu were deleted unused; the app's point-anchored ContextMenu.vue is built on ui/dropdown-menu instead.
P110 converted every .p-* rule, remaining hand-rolled Studio/Space/workbench style blocks, and kira-ui's controls.css onto Tailwind utilities, @theme tokens or shadcn-vue variants.

packages/theme/src/primitives.css is residue only (75 lines, down from 1013): the single rule .p-input.is-grow, which has no Tailwind utility equivalent and is kept unlayered so it keeps beating a layered utility by construction.
packages/workbench/src/workbench.css contains only two non-comment lines: importing @theme/base.css (the compiled Tailwind root) and an @source for the package's own scan.

packages/git-ui/src compiles in Kira Space's own Tailwind root (P245); the kv: prefix, git-ui's second root and the --vscode-*/--kv-* token layer are gone, and its only CSS is theme/git.css imported by Space's styles.css.
Fetching a new shadcn-vue component set is a direct-registry pull, not shadcn-vue add; the procedure is in docs/DEV_ENVIRONMENT.md's shadcn-vue section.

Empty/EmptyMedia/EmptyTitle/EmptyDescription (components/ui/empty/) is the one empty-state component; Alert with class empty-state was a misuse (role=alert on a merely empty list) and was converted onto it.

Row components (TreeRow, CollectionRow, RepoTreeRow, RepoSearchRow) take a class prop and own their selection ternary instead of using shared .tree-row/.selected/.sticky CSS; stateClass is selected ? 'bg-select' : sticky ? 'bg-bg hover:bg-hover' : 'hover:bg-hover', so selected beats hover by ternary order, not CSS specificity.
Row components receive sticky as a prop so a row inside a sticky layer paints its own sticky background instead of the parent reaching in.

In packages/git-ui dialogs (P131 Part 1), all 14 dialogs plus PreflightPrediction.vue moved from Kui* components to Dialog/Button/Input/Textarea/Checkbox/RadioGroup/NativeSelect/Label, and the shadcn-vue radio-group set was pulled in.

Pair non-native-input-like controls in git-ui dialogs with an explicit useId()-driven for/id, because biome's noLabelWithoutControl cannot see through a wrapped component's inheritAttrs: false to the native element.
Point-anchored DropdownMenus must pass prioritize-position so reka's Popper flips before it shifts, because shift alone can clamp overflow to zero against a 0×0 anchor and leave flip with no signal.

P131 Part 2 moved git-ui's App.vue, 23 of 30 components/*.vue, refBadges.ts and rowMenuModel.ts onto @theme/components/*, with Popover (gaining outside-click/Escape dismissal), DropdownMenu, ToggleGroup, InputGroup, NativeSelect, Checkbox, Badge (chip variant, REF_BADGE_CLASS), Button and Tooltip.

AttributeTooltip.vue (moved from workbench to theme) is one hoisted instance per list/grid container, mounted as a sibling and never a child of any container SlickGrid's init() can empty; it reads a data-kira-tip attribute on descendants, replacing v-kui-tooltip and refBadges.ts's data-kui-tip writes.
TooltipProvider, moved from workbench to theme, wraps both packages/git-ui mount roots via a new MountRoot.vue in main.ts's mount(), replacing the package's per-root KuiTooltip/initTooltips.
P131 Part 3 converted packages/git-ui/src/components/review/*, so packages/git-ui is fully on shadcn-vue with no Kui* import left.
@kira/kira-ui was deleted in P267; before that it was reduced to floatingPosition.ts after P264 deleted KuiColumnResizeHandle.

title: Renderer security surface
lines: internal/shell/security.go is the single module owning the renderer security posture under Wails; Harden() returns the posture and window.go's Options is its only caller.
Harden() denies every permission except clipboard reads, sets JavaScriptCanOpenWindowsAutomatically false, and leaves EnableFileDrop and OpenInspectorOnStartup false.

Under Wails the webview is native WKWebView rather than bundled Chromium, so most Electron hardening switches (contextIsolation, sandbox, nodeIntegration, webviewTag, WebGL off, the seven disable-* switches, the Electron fuses) have no subject.
The renderer reaches Go only through generated bindings and the engine stream; there is no contextBridge/window.kira surface and no Node in the webview.
DevTools are disabled in packaged builds via the Go build tag -tags production, already set by apps/kira-studio/build/darwin/Taskfile.yml.

On macOS and Linux only camera and microphone permissions are enforced by Wails (v3.0.0-beta.28 consults Permissions for getUserMedia only); geolocation, notifications and clipboard are not consulted, and the macOS clipboard answer is WebKit's user-gesture heuristics.

window.open denial is only partial under Wails: JavaScriptCanOpenWindowsAutomatically=false denies JS-initiated windows, but there is no per-request handler (no WKUIDelegate createWebViewWithConfiguration:).

There is no navigation lock to the base URL under Wails on darwin because there is no navigation-policy delegate; this is a known real loss versus Electron's will-frame-navigate guard plus fuses and is recorded, not mitigated.

Wails exposes no spellcheck control, so spellcheck="false" is set on the field itself in the renderer, because the connection dialog's password field becomes plain type="text" once the eye toggle reveals it.

Assets are no longer served over file://: apps/kira-studio/main.go embeds frontend/dist and serves it through a plain Go http.Handler (AssetOptions.Handler), so the file:// module-CORS trap and grantFileProtocolExtraPrivileges no longer apply.
Every externally-openable link in the git UI (packages/git-ui) is a button calling a host capability, never an anchor; there is no window.open or target="_blank".
Git UI external-link surfaces are gated on capabilities.openExternal and render a plain span when the host does not report it.

PR links go through pr.browserUrl/GitHubService.OpenPullRequestURL, while URLs in commit message bodies go through the generic link.openExternal, because a PR URL is composed server-side from app-controlled data but a commit-body URL is untrusted content.
LinkService.OpenExternal refuses anything that is not a well-formed http/https URL with a non-empty host before Browser.OpenURL sees it, and git-ui host handlers do equivalent shape validation.

The PR URL host check is gitsession.IsGitHubHost (github.com plus any host gh's Discovery has authenticated against), shared by composer and validator rather than two hand-rolled allowlists, because the previous hardcoded literal broke GitHub Enterprise Server.

packages/git-ui moved fully to Kira Space (P100); Kira Studio's frontend no longer depends on it. The linkOpenExternal wrapper lives in packages/workbench/src/bridge/createCoreControl.ts, with git UI as its only caller, binding Space's bridge/link.go.
Kira Studio has its own LinkService (apps/kira-studio/internal/bridge/link.go, P260) for the Docker registry button, called from apps/kira-studio/frontend/src/docker/context.ts.

The WKWebView is not configurable beyond the existing options: MacWebviewPreferences in Wails v3.0.0-beta.28 has ten fields with no compositing or tiling knob, the WKWebViewConfiguration is built inside one cgo block with no hook, and macOS has no engine-flags escape hatch (unlike WindowsOptions for WebView2).
The coverage-rect/tile-pooling behaviour lives in WebCore, below anything public WKWebView/WKWebViewConfiguration/WKPreferences expose, so NativeWindow() access gives nothing to set.
Re-check WKWebView configurability after any Wails version bump, because the repo keeps moving through betas.
Autofill is controlled renderer-side: there are zero form elements, and AutocompleteField.vue (packages/workbench/src/components) explicitly sets autocomplete: 'off'.

The clipboard permission is an allowlist rather than deny-all, because denying clipboard reads throws in copyText (packages/workbench/src/behaviour/clipboard.ts), which 23 files import plus the grid's paste path.
Hardware acceleration is deliberately left on because the grid's scroll budget depends on GPU compositing.
window.confirm() is not used; destructive actions are gated through the in-page confirm store (packages/workbench/src/state/confirmDialog.ts plus ConfirmDialog.vue).

The security posture is guarded by internal/shell/security_test.go and menu_test.go (TestBuildMenuAcceleratorsAllParse); no Wails analogue of the old hardening.spec.ts e2e exists because nothing is left for it to assert.
The macOS-only behaviours (WebKit clipboard gesture heuristics and the absent navigation delegate) have no automated coverage on any platform the repo's CI runs.

title: 6. Known gaps
lines: The Kafka native-module packaging gap is closed: Kafka went native in Go (P58e M9), and P58f M10 deleted the Node engine, build:engine, and every check probing for @confluentinc/kafka-javascript.
The build is ad-hoc signed only (identity -), so it is not distributable outside the machine that built it; SPEC.md §3 defers signing/notarization past v1.
wails3 tool sign [--notarize] is available via darwin:sign/darwin:sign:notarize tasks but is wired into nothing.
bun run package:studio runs darwin:package:dmg, producing both the .app and a styled DMG, and scripts/sign-bundle.sh ad-hoc signs both.
The DMG window is 540×380 with the app at 28% and the /Applications shortcut at 72% of its width; positions come from wails3 tool package itself.
The DMG volume icon and the image's Finder icon are both darwin/icons.icns, and darwin/dmg-background.png is a flat gradient in the app icon's palette with an arrow between the icon positions.
The scaffolded dmg-file-icon.icns/.png (Wails-branded drive artwork) were deleted.
An ad-hoc-signed DMG is still Gatekeeper-blocked on first launch, with a workaround in §4's checklist.
The bundle has no Assets.car; the app icon comes from darwin/icons.icns alone, regenerated from appicon.png and appicon.icon via wails3 task common:generate:icons.
Building an asset catalog needs Apple's actool, which ships with full Xcode and not Command Line Tools, and fails silently when absent.

CFBundleIconName resolves against Assets.car before CFBundleIconFile falls back to icons.icns, so the stale scaffolded Wails Assets.car made packaged apps show the old Wails icon; both the file and the CFBundleIconName key were removed.
Reintroduce Assets.car and the CFBundleIconName key together or neither, because wails3 update build-assets adds the key back automatically whenever an Assets.car is present.
appicon.icon is kept for regenerating a catalog on a machine with Xcode; without a catalog macOS composes no appearance variants (dark, tinted) from the icon.

icon.json was changed to a single layer with 1.0 scale, no recolor, and non-specular, because the scaffolded settings suited a small monochrome glyph, not a full-color pre-composed 1024×1024 icon; it is unverified beyond wails3 generate icons accepting it.

title: 1. Building locally
lines: Building Kira Studio locally requires macOS arm64, Bun, Go (go.mod: 1.27.0) and Xcode command-line tools; bun install, go mod download and the pinned wails3 CLI install themselves.

bun run package:studio and bun run dev:studio both run bun run setup first (via prepackage:studio/predev:studio); it is scripts/setup.sh, the single entry point for everything a fresh clone needs before building.
bun run package:studio installs everything, then runs wails3 task darwin:package:dmg, then scripts/sign-bundle.sh.

setup.sh installs the pinned wails3 CLI with GOTOOLCHAIN pinned to go.mod's own go directive, never auto, because auto resolves the toolchain from Wails' own floor and silently degrades the bindings generator's type-checker.
setup.sh reinstalls wails3 only when the pinned version changed or when the installed binary's build toolchain is older than the go.mod directive.

setup.sh regenerates bindings via wails3 task common:generate:bindings for both Kira Studio and Kira Space (apps/kira-space), each gated on its own stamp (apps/<app>/.task/bindings.stamp) and bindings directory presence.
The frontend bridge files (apps/kira-studio/frontend/src/bridge/*.ts) import generated bindings directly, so bun run build:studio fails without them.
setup.sh does only what is missing on each run; bun run setup runs just the install step.
apps/kira-studio/{bin,frontend/dist,frontend/bindings} are gitignored.
The shipped artifact is apps/kira-studio/bin/Kira Studio.dmg, a styled, ad-hoc-signed disk image holding the app and an /Applications shortcut.

apps/kira-studio/bin/Kira Studio.app is the ad-hoc-signed bundle the dmg is built from; it is still produced and used for local runs but no longer ships. bin/Kira Studio is the bare Go binary it is assembled around.
No app artifact carries a .vsix, because the VS Code extension was removed in P243 Part 2.
No .zip is produced anywhere; the release workflow uploads the .dmg.
The bundle's Contents/MacOS/Kira Studio filename, space included, must equal CFBundleExecutable or the bundle neither launches nor codesigns.
The bundle has Info.plist with CFBundleIdentifier com.kirathecat.kira-studio and CFBundleName/CFBundleExecutable "Kira Studio"; Resources/icons.icns is the only icon and no Assets.car ships.
The bundle has no runtime/ subtree since P58f M10; the compiled Go binary is the whole app, and create:app:bundle no longer asserts or copies runtime/{node,engine}.

bun run dev:studio (cd apps/kira-studio && wails3 task dev) launches a native window with hot reload: a blocking common:build:frontend for the embedded bundle, then common:dev:frontend (Vite dev server) in the background for HMR.
wails3 task darwin:run builds and runs a Kira Studio.dev.app from build/darwin/Info.dev.plist without packaging.
